speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing fever and abdominal tenderness after giving birth; have you had any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or changes in your baby's breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The history of a prolonged labor, combined with decreased bowel sounds and uterine tenderness, makes me concerned about complications like postpartum endometritis or an ileus. Have you experienced any pain in your lower abdomen that radiates to your legs, or do you have a history of pelvic inflammatory disease?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Uterine Torsion (or severe postpartum endometritis with ileus). The combination of prolonged labor, uterine tenderness, fever, decreased bowel sounds, and urinary frequency in a patient with a large baby (11 lbs) strongly suggests the uterus has twisted on its axis. I recommend immediate imaging to confirm. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.
